newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends up, Dec breaks nearby resistance.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends up, Dec breaks nearby resistance.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed firmer as a late-session bout of speculative buying fueled the benchmark December contract over resistance and to the day's highs, floor sources said.
The benchmark December contract closed 0.58 cent firmer at 74.78 cents per lb, having ranged from 74.85 to 74.15 cents. The rest of the board finished 0.40 to 0.60 cent higher.

Prices drifted barely over unchanged for most of the session as December remained below resistance. Speculative buying just ahead of the close carried the contract over resistance and to the day's highs.

The market is expected to follow-through on Friday as December should test its next upside target of 75.00 cents. A move over the key level would attract substantial buying by the funds and lift the contract sharply higher, analysts said.
"If we punch through 75.00 cents it's worth another 50-100 points," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said.
Producer scale-up selling could limit the rally, however.

The market got an early boost from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's weekly export and sales report. The USDA said 135,000 480-bales of upland cotton were sold and 94,200 bales of upland cotton were shipped in the week ended July 10.
The market looks toward the USDA's August supply and demand report, the first survey-based estimates of the 1997/98 crop.
Support remained at 74.00 cents followed by 72.00 cents in December.
An estimated 6,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Wednesday's official 5,031 lots.
